documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 y/o woman establishing primary care. Started a graduate program this fall and moved to Easthampton.

Type 1 diabetes: diagnosed in 2019, on basal-bolus insulin from the start. Glargine 20 units at bedtime, aspart 8 units with meals, has a glucagon kit. Sees an outside endocrinology group about twice a year and wants to stay with them; they write all her insulin scripts. Fingersticks several times a day. Denies any severe lows, ED visits or DKA since diagnosis. Runs most days.

PMH: T1DM as above. PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18. Meds as above. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt with Hashimoto thyroiditis; paternal grandfather with type 2 diabetes.
SH: grad student, lives with a roommate. Never smoker. Alcohol rarely, less than one drink a month. No drugs.

ROS negative in full: no polyuria, vision change, numbness, chest pain, dyspnea, GI or GU complaints.

Exam: well appearing, vitals as charted. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, insulin sites on abdomen and thighs without lipohypertrophy. Skin clear. Feet: no lesions or calluses, DP and PT pulses 2+, monofilament and vibration intact bilaterally. Neuro grossly normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes, by her report well controlled. Continue regimen per endocrinology. A1c, CMP, lipids, TSH (family history of Hashimoto plus T1DM), urine microalbumin/creatinine, CBC. Celiac screen with tTG IgA once since we have no record of one. Will request her endocrinology notes.
2. Health maintenance: HIV and hep C screening today. Tdap given, last one was around age 11. Flu and COVID booster in a few weeks when the fall vaccines are in. Old student health records requested for Pap and vaccine history. Yearly dilated eye exam: she will book with an optometrist.
3. Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed.

documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 09/10/2024
Re: Abigail Lemieux, DOB 10/08/1999

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Lemieux for her scheduled follow-up of type 1 diabetes. She has used basal-bolus insulin for five years now and control remains good: her most recent A1c is 6.8%. No hypoglycemic episodes since her last visit.

Current regimen: insulin glargine 20 units subcutaneously at bedtime; insulin aspart 8 units subcutaneously before meals; glucagon 1 mg IM emergency kit on hand.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: maternal aunt with Hashimoto thyroiditis; paternal grandfather with type 2 diabetes.
Social: graduate student, never smoker, drinks rarely. She is a committed runner and is about to start marathon training, with daily runs that will go beyond an hour.

Her main question today was how to handle insulin and food once the long runs start.

Vitals within normal limits. Examination unremarkable.

Assessment and plan:
Type 1 diabetes, well controlled. Doses unchanged. We went through exercise planning in detail: check glucose before she sets out, periodically during any run longer than an hour, and again afterward and at bedtime on long-run days; carry fast-acting carbohydrate on every run; she may take a smaller aspart dose with the meal before a long run, using her own judgment and her logs. Late lows after long runs were discussed.
Return in 6 months.

With thanks,
Outside endocrinology group

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 05/09/2025, 17:40.

CC: L ear pain x3 days.

HPI: 25F with type 1 diabetes on insulin, well controlled, followed by endocrinology (last seen about 8 months ago). Three days of left ear pain, much worse when she tugs on the ear lobe. Ear feels plugged and she hears less on that side. No discharge from the ear. No fever, chills, headache, dizziness or facial weakness. Went swimming in a lake about 5 days ago.

PMH: T1DM. PSH: third molar extraction at 18.
Meds: insulin glargine 20 units SC qhs; insulin aspart 8 units SC before meals; glucagon 1 mg IM PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt Hashimoto; paternal grandfather T2DM.
SH: graduate student. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals reviewed, afebrile. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. L external auditory canal erythematous and swollen nearly shut, marked tenderness over the tragus; TM cannot be seen past the swelling. No discharge. No periauricular swelling or mastoid tenderness. Facial nerve intact. R ear normal. No cervical adenopathy.

Data: fingerstick glucose 180 mg/dL.

MDM: painful otitis externa of the left ear in an insulin-dependent diabetic after freshwater exposure. Given diabetes, treated as malignant otitis externa with antipseudomonal coverage and prompt ENT evaluation.

Dx: Malignant otitis externa, left ear.

Rx: ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO BID; ofloxacin otic 0.3% 10 drops L ear BID x14 days. Keep the ear dry, no swimming. Monitor glucose more often while ill.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Follow up with ENT within days, call PCP Monday. Return for fever, spreading swelling, facial weakness, severe headache or worsening pain.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I went to the ER last night for my left ear. It's been hurting since Tuesday and I can barely hear out of it. They said it's an outer ear infection and because I have diabetes they called it malignant otitis externa?? They gave me cipro pills and ear drops and said I need to see ENT soon. I don't have an ENT. Sugars have been running a little higher than usual. Pain is about the same this morning.

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Keep taking both, keep the ear dry, and keep a closer eye on your sugars; infections and cipro can both push them around. I'll do a video visit with you Monday morning and get ENT lined up. If you get a fever, swelling around the ear, a headache that won't quit or any weakness in your face, go back to the ER.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home in Easthampton, identity confirmed.

Seen in a regional ED Friday evening for 3 days of left ear pain after lake swimming 5 days before that. Per her and her discharge paperwork: canal swollen shut, tragal tenderness, TM not visible, fingerstick 180. Diagnosed with malignant otitis externa given her T1DM; started ciprofloxacin 750 mg BID and ofloxacin otic drops. ED record not yet received.

Today: day 3 of treatment. Pain about the same, maybe slightly less at night. Ear still plugged, hearing muffled on the left. No drainage, no fever, no headache, no facial droop. Glucose running higher than her usual; no lows. Taking cipro with food, drops twice a day.

Observed on video: comfortable, no visible swelling behind or in front of the ear, face symmetric.

A/P
1. Malignant otitis externa, left, on ciprofloxacin and ofloxacin drops from the ED. Needs ENT this week given diabetes. Urgent ENT referral placed and called through.
2. T1DM: expect some rise in sugars with infection; correction per her endo plan, call endo if readings stay high or she has ketones. Cipro can also cause lows, keep checking.
3. Cipro and tendons: hold the long runs until the course is done, stop and call for any heel or calf pain.
Return precautions reviewed.

reports.text:
Technique: axial thin-section images through both temporal bones without intravenous contrast, with coronal reformats.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Soft-tissue thickening of the left external auditory canal with narrowing of the canal lumen. The bony canal walls are intact with no erosion. The left middle ear cavity and ossicles are normal. Left mastoid air cells are well aerated and clear. No soft-tissue collection in the periauricular region. Skull base and temporomandibular joint normal. The right temporal bone is normal.
reports.conclusion: Soft-tissue thickening and narrowing of the left external auditory canal without bony erosion. Middle ear and mastoid clear.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group
Date of consultation: 05/14/2025
Referring: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Abigail Lemieux, a 25-year-old graduate student with type 1 diabetes, for left ear pain treated in an ED on 5/9 as malignant otitis externa.

She developed left otalgia after swimming in a lake, with fullness and reduced hearing. On ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily and ofloxacin otic drops since 5/9; pain now slowly easing. No otorrhea, fever, vertigo or facial weakness.

Meds: glargine 20 units qhs, aspart 8 units before meals, glucagon kit, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin otic.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: left canal edematous and erythematous; tragal tenderness and pain with traction on the pinna. Under the microscope the canal was debrided and a sample sent for culture; no granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction. After cleaning the TM could be glimpsed only partly. A wick was placed. Right ear normal. Facial nerve function intact and symmetric. No cervical lymphadenopathy.

CT temporal bones today: soft-tissue thickening of the left canal without bony erosion; middle ear and mastoid clear.
ESR 41.
Culture (final 5/17): Pseudomonas aeruginosa, ciprofloxacin sensitive.

Impression: early necrotizing (malignant) otitis externa, left, in a patient with type 1 diabetes. Imaging shows no bone involvement.

Plan:
- Continue ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily for a total of six weeks from the start on 5/9.
- Ofloxacin drops to finish 14 days; wick to come out on its own or at a nurse check.
- Strict water precautions.
- Good glucose control with her endocrinologist.
- Return in about five weeks with a repeat ESR; sooner for worsening pain, drainage, headache or facial weakness.

Sincerely,
Otolaryngology

Outside otolaryngology group

Ms. Lemieux returns six weeks into treatment for left necrotizing otitis externa. Pain resolved within the first two weeks. Hearing back to normal by her report. Finished the drops in May; wick fell out on its own. Tolerated ciprofloxacin without tendon pain. Sugars back to her usual.

Exam: left canal healed, skin normal, no debris, no granulation. TM intact, mobile, normal landmarks. Right ear normal. Facial nerve intact.

ESR today 12, down from 41.

Impression: left necrotizing otitis externa, resolved after six weeks of oral ciprofloxacin.

Plan: stop ciprofloxacin today. Keep the ear dry while swimming for the rest of the summer (ear plugs). Return as needed; she knows to come back promptly for any recurrence of ear pain given her diabetes.

Otolaryngology

conditions.label: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with hypoglycemia with coma

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 05/17/2026, arrival 11:05 by ambulance.

CC: hypoglycemia, found unresponsive.

HPI: 26F with type 1 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin, followed by endocrinology; seen here a year ago for an ear infection. Roommate found her unresponsive in her room late this morning and called 911. She had been up very late studying and had not eaten breakfast. Per EMS run sheet: diaphoretic and unresponsive on their arrival, fingerstick glucose 38; glucagon 1 mg IM given at once, and she began to wake within minutes. By arrival here she is awake, oriented and answering questions, amnestic for the event. Took her usual glargine 20 units at bedtime. Did not take any aspart this morning since she didn't eat. No alcohol. No recent illness, no extra exercise yesterday. No seizure activity witnessed, no incontinence, no injury per roommate.

PMH: T1DM; left malignant otitis externa 2025, resolved.
Meds: insulin glargine 20 units SC qhs; insulin aspart 8 units SC with meals; glucagon 1 mg IM PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: graduate student, lives with a roommate. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Awake, alert, oriented x3, conversant. Skin warm, drying. No head or tongue injury. Pupils equal and reactive. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal, gait steady.

Data: EMS fingerstick 38. ED point-of-care glucose on arrival 96.

Course: given juice and a meal tray, which she finished. Repeat glucose checks over the observation period stayed in range. Glucagon had brought her glucose back up in the field.

Impression: severe hypoglycemia with loss of consciousness in type 1 diabetes, from a missed meal after bedtime basal insulin.

Disposition: observed and discharged home the same afternoon with her roommate. Insulin doses unchanged. Eat before studying late, check glucose at bedtime and on waking. Keep her glucagon kit with her; roommate should know how to use it. Follow up with primary care and endocrinology this week. Return for any further severe low.

Advised no driving until she has been seen. ED record requested.

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after ED visit 5/17. ED record received yesterday and reviewed.

Sunday morning her roommate found her unresponsive after she had stayed up late studying and skipped breakfast. EMS: diaphoretic, unresponsive, fingerstick 38; glucagon 1 mg IM, woke quickly. 96 on ED arrival, ate, observed, sent home same day. Her first severe low since diagnosis; she had none at her last endo visit and none before.

Since then: feels back to normal. Eating on schedule. Checking before bed and when she wakes; no readings she'd call low. Same doses: glargine 20 at bedtime, aspart 8 before meals. Has her endocrinology appointment in June and left a message with them Monday. Her own glucagon kit was never used and is in date; she has shown her roommate where it is.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, well. No bruising or injury. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Severe hypoglycemia with loss of consciousness, single episode, explained by a missed meal on her usual bedtime glargine. Resolved. No dose change today; dosing stays with endocrinology, who I am messaging.
- Don't skip meals on glargine nights, especially during exam weeks; eat something when studying late.
- Check glucose at bedtime and on waking, and before any drive.
- Roommate to be shown how to give the glucagon kit, not just where it is.
- No driving until endocrinology has gone over the episode with her.
2. T1DM otherwise stable.
Physical due in the fall.

documents.title: Message to Endocrinology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the endocrinology group following Abigail Lemieux (DOB 10/08/1999):

FYI, she was seen in a regional ED on 5/17 for severe hypoglycemia with loss of consciousness after a missed breakfast; EMS glucose 38, glucagon IM, 96 on arrival, discharged the same day. I saw her today and she is well. Current doses unchanged (glargine 20 units qhs, aspart 8 units AC). I have deferred any regimen change to you and advised no driving until you have reviewed the episode. She has a visit with you in June. ED record attached.

Primary care

documents.body: Thanks for the update, glad it's been quiet. We haven't gotten their note, so I'll ask them for a copy. See you at your physical.

documents.body: Hi! Can I book my yearly physical for September? Tuesdays are best for me, mornings.

documents.title: RE: Scheduling my physical

documents.body: You're booked for Tuesday 9/22 at 8:30 am. Please come fasting; labs will be drawn at the visit. Flu and COVID shots should be in by then too.
